pharm: Antihypertensive vasodilator; also reduces nightmares in PTSD (off-label) and aids BPH symptoms
quick: 1 mg BID-TID, titrate to 6-15 mg/day (max 40 mg/day)
Category C; use only if clearly needed
Start low; usual doses generally tolerated
summary: Prazosin is a selective alpha-1 adrenergic blocker indicated for hypertension. It lowers blood pressure by reducing peripheral vascular resistance, generally without reflex tachycardia. A notable first-dose phenomenon (marked postural hypotension/syncope) can occur, especially with the initial dose, dose increases, or addition of other antihypertensives. It is also widely used off-label for PTSD-associated nightmares and BPH symptoms. Initiate at low dose, usually at bedtime, and titrate gradually.

dosage.d: 1 mg two or three times daily
dosage.n: First dose at bedtime to limit first-dose syncope

dosage.d: Up to 20 mg/day (rarely up to 40 mg/day)
dosage.n: Doses >20 mg usually do not increase efficacy

dosage.d: Reduce to 1-2 mg TID, then re-titrate
1 mg at bedtime, titrate to ~3-15 mg

admin: Give the first dose at bedtime to minimize first-dose hypotension/syncope
Titrate gradually based on blood pressure response
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness
Reduce dose and re-titrate when adding another antihypertensive or diuretic
moa: Selective post-synaptic alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist; blocks norepinephrine-mediated vasoconstriction in arterioles and veins, decreasing total peripheral resistance and lowering blood pressure, typically without reflex tachycardia. Also relaxes prostatic and bladder neck smooth muscle.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to quinazolines, prazosin, or any inert ingredient
relative: Volume depletion or concurrent diuretic/antihypertensive therapy
Planned cataract surgery (intraoperative floppy iris syndrome risk)

preg: Pregnancy Category C. No human fetal abnormalities reported in limited use with a beta-blocker for severe hypertension; animal data show decreased litter size at very high doses. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: Excreted in small amounts in human milk; exercise caution when administered to a nursing woman.
renal: Start at a low dose; usual doses are generally tolerated in renal impairment. Titrate to response.
hepatic: Use with caution; consider a lower starting dose as hepatic impairment may increase exposure.

major: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - additive hypotension
moderate: Diuretics - enhanced hypotensive effect (reduce prazosin dose)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May increase urinary metabolites of norepinephrine (VMA) and MHPG - relevant if screening for pheochromocytoma

monitoring: Symptoms of dizziness/syncope, especially after first dose and dose changes
Therapeutic response (BP goal or nightmare frequency for off-label use)
counsel: Take the first dose at bedtime; may cause fainting
Rise slowly from sitting or lying down
Avoid driving or hazardous tasks until you know how it affects you
Report fainting, palpitations, or prolonged erection (priapism)
Inform your eye surgeon you take this drug before cataract surgery
Do not stop abruptly without advice
pearls: First-dose phenomenon: marked postural hypotension/syncope within 30-90 min - start low at bedtime
Preferred over benzodiazepines for PTSD nightmares in many guidelines (off-label)
No reflex tachycardia, unlike direct vasodilators
Associated with intraoperative floppy iris syndrome - alert ophthalmologist
missed: Take when remembered unless near the next dose, then skip and resume schedule; do not double up. If several doses missed, restart at the low initial dose (first-dose effect may recur).
overdose: Profound hypotension, drowsiness, depressed reflexes, tachycardia or bradycardia. Management: place supine/Trendelenburg, IV fluids for volume expansion, vasopressors if needed; supportive care; not effectively dialyzed (highly protein bound).
